assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a genuine invention: a new kind of semiconductor laser based on intersubband transitions in engineered quantum-well heterostructures, built layer by layer with molecular beam epitaxy. It opened mid-infrared and terahertz sources that were not practical before, and it is now used in gas sensing, spectroscopy and security applications. From an instrument and materials viewpoint it is the clearest case of an original device being demonstrated and then widely verified.
assessment.attribution: The 1994 demonstration came from the Bell Labs team around Faist and Capasso, with Cho's epitaxial growth indispensable to realizing the structure. The credited trio matches the core of the original work. Others at Bell Labs (for example Sirtori, Sivco, Hutchinson) also contributed, which I cannot resolve from the supplied credit, and the earlier Kazarinov-Suris proposal of intersubband gain is a historical precursor.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of independent reproduction, commercial availability and broad application. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the Kazarinov-Suris 1971 proposal affects the priority argument.
Whether other Bell Labs co-authors should share the credit; I rely on my recollection rather than verified records.
Some may see it as engineering rather than physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on Katori's magic-wavelength idea and its experimental realization, brought fractional clock uncertainty to the 10^-18 level. This is a new measurement capability that opens a door to relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a future redefinition of the second. It is an original idea backed by repeated, precise experimental demonstration.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early clocks; Jun Ye's group made the decisive precision demonstrations. A two-person configuration is clean. Contributions by Hall and Hänsch to the frequency comb are already recognized (2005), and trapped-ion clock work is a separate line.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation from several labs worldwide and a clear path to application. Timing is appropriate, though redefinition of the second is still pending.
uncertainties: Overlap with Jun Ye's other nominated work (ultracold molecules) is a separate matter.
Boundary against ion-clock pioneers is not settled in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond created a room-temperature solid-state spin system that can be read out with light. It is a tool that lets people see and sense magnetic fields, temperature and strain at the nanoscale, including in biological and materials settings, which is the type of door-opening instrument I value.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group first demonstrated optical detection of a single NV spin (1997), and Jelezko with Wrachtrup showed coherent control (2004). These are the original experiments. Lukin's contribution is substantial for theory and sensing applications, but his work is more of a later development; I would not include him for the original discovery.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many groups and now widely used, with active commercial development. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Whether the sensing applications should be rewarded together with the original single-spin detection.
Role of Lukin and other early groups (for example Gruber et al. co-authors) is uncertain in my memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened the field of moire quantum materials: the Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction was followed by the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity. It shows that a simple twist angle acts as a tuning knob for strongly correlated phases, and has produced a very large body of work.
assessment.attribution: The theoretical prediction is Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011); the decisive experiments came from Jarillo-Herrero's group. The first author of the experimental papers, Yuan Cao, is not in the credited list, which is a real concern about whether the people who did the original experiments are fully recognized. A prize limited to three would need a careful choice.
assessment.maturity: Rapid and extensive independent confirmation across many groups, although the interpretation of the superconductivity is not settled. It may be slightly early but it is not premature as a discovery.
uncertainties: Credit for the experimental discovery among junior researchers who are not named.
Mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Possible earlier theoretical work on twisted-bilayer flat bands.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-halide perovskite solar cells went from a dye-sensitised curiosity to above 25 percent efficiency in little over a decade. The materials and device physics are significant for energy and for humanity, which is the kind of benefit the Nobel will consider. It is also a materials story that I know from the microscopy side.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell in 2009, Park produced the solid-state cell in 2012, and Snaith's group showed the mesosuperstructured and planar architectures. This is a plausible three-person configuration, though Gratzel and others contributed to the solid-state architecture and the credit is disputed in the community.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency has been confirmed independently and repeatedly, but long-term stability and lead toxicity remain open, so it is arguably early for a prize.
uncertainties: Stability and commercial viability not yet demonstrated at scale.
Whether the prize would be seen as physics rather than chemistry or materials science.
Priority disputes between early dye-sensitised work and the later solid-state devices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions (1995) was the experimental breakthrough that made magnetic read heads and MRAM practical. It is a clear, verified discovery with significant technological impact in data storage.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 1995, which supports a two-person prize. Parkin's later MgO-based work with very high TMR is an important improvement, but in the spirit of crediting the original experiment rather than the better later one, I would not include him as first choice. Julliere's 1975 low-temperature result is a precursor.
assessment.maturity: Mature; the technology has been in hard drives for years. The spintronics area was already recognized by the 2007 prize, which may reduce the appetite for a second award in a neighbouring area.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize.
Whether Parkin and the MgO developments should be included in the same award.
Role of Julliere's precursor.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetars link a theoretical prediction of ultra-strongly magnetised neutron stars to the observation of soft gamma repeaters and anomalous X-ray pulsars. The 1998 timing of SGR 1806-20 supporting a field around 10^15 G was an observational result, and later events such as giant flares and the 2020 SGR 1935 burst strengthened it. It enlarges our understanding of the universe.
assessment.attribution: Duncan and Thompson made the 1992 prediction and Kouveliotou led the observational confirmation, which matches an experiment-theory pairing. It also would recognise a woman at the centre of the discovery. Other observers (for example Hurley, Mereghetti) contributed to the empirical picture and I cannot verify their relative roles.
assessment.maturity: Good, with multiple independent confirmations, though the link to fast radio bursts is still being explored.
uncertainties: Contributions of other observers (Hurley, Mereghetti, Paczynski's earlier ideas) are uncertain.
Whether astrophysics of this type fits the physics prize better than previous cases.
Detailed field estimates depend on model assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first observation of the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological-insulator thin films (2013) was a demanding experiment built on molecular beam epitaxy and low-temperature transport. It displays quantized Hall resistance without an external field and is a tool for dissipationless edge transport and metrology.
assessment.attribution: Xue's group carried out the original experiment; the theoretical prediction for magnetic topological insulators came from Fang, Dai and collaborators, while Haldane's 1988 model already earned a prize in 2016. Because the topological part is already recognized, I would limit credit to the experimentalist and I am unsure that this is fair to the theory side.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by several groups, though the quantization temperature remained very low for a long time. The topological insulator area is partially recognized already.
uncertainties: Overlap with 2016 prize for topological phases.
Fair credit between Xue's group, the theorists and the Kane-Mele-related predictions.
Practical relevance for devices still limited.
